html:
An army officer who ruled the Congo, which he renamed Zaire, from 1965 to 1997. He was a sergeant in the colonial army and a journalist before independence.

As army chief during the Congo Crisis, he pushed aside Patrice Lumumba in 1960 and played a part in his handover to his killers. In 1965 he seized power for good.

  • His campaign of "authenticity" swapped colonial names for African ones: Léopoldville became Kinshasa, the country Zaire, and he renamed himself Mobutu Sese Seko.
  • He was a key Western ally in the Cold War, backed by the United States against Soviet-supported movements in Angola.
  • He hosted the Rumble in the Jungle in 1974 to show off his country.

His rule became a byword for kleptocracy, government by theft. His circle grew rich while roads and services decayed. After the Cold War, Western support dried up. The refugee crisis after the Rwandan genocide brought war to the east, and in 1997 rebels led by Laurent-Désiré Kabila, backed by Rwanda and Uganda, drove him out. He died in exile in Morocco months later.
sum: An army officer who ruled the Congo, which he renamed Zaire, from 1965 to 1997. He was a sergeant in the colonial army and a journalist before independence.
